Record FY2025 revenue of $2,515.3M (+85.5%) - CEO John Fieldly called it a 'defining year'; revenue growth was primarily driven by $1,001.9M of Alani Nu revenue (Q2-Q4) plus $55.6M from Rockstar Energy and 7.5% CELSIUS brand growth.

Celsius Holdings built a scaled three-brand 'Modern Energy' portfolio (CELSIUS, Alani Nu, Rockstar Energy) and reached an ~20% dollar share of the US energy drink category in Q4 2025 as PepsiCo's energy category captain.
Q4 revenue grew 117% to $721.6M; Q4 adjusted EBITDA $134.1M (+113%); FY adjusted EBITDA $619.6M (+142%, 24.6% margin); Q4 adjusted diluted EPS $0.26 (+86%), FY $1.34 (+91%).

CELSIUS brand revenue declined ~8% in Q4 due to anticipated, temporary integration-related timing dynamics and distributor order sequencing - a short-term misalignment between shipments, depletions and promotions; US tracked retail sales rose +13% over the same 13 weeks, so the decline is 'not reflective of underlying retail demand.'
A net positive ~$25M impact in Q4 2025 from the Alani Nu load-in to PepsiCo offsetting the CELSIUS brand timing differences.

Q4 GAAP gross margin compressed 280 bps to 47.4% on Rockstar dilution, higher integration costs and tariffs, partially offset by billbacks, improved outbound freight and favorable product/pack mix; FY gross margin still improved 20 bps to 50.4%.

FY GAAP net income fell 26% to $108.0M and FY GAAP diluted EPS declined 44% to $0.25, pressured by $327M of distributor termination costs, $60M of acquisition-related costs and $49.0M of interest expense (vs $39.3M of net interest income in FY2024).

Total distributor buyout obligation recorded by year-end 2025 was ~$327.5M ($246.7M in Q3 + $80.8M in Q4); balance sheet shows $141.1M restricted cash, $264.1M accrued distributor termination fees, $669.9M long-term debt and $907.6M of newly issued Series B convertible preferred stock.

Alani Nu had a record Q4 of ~$370.0M, benefiting from ongoing demand plus increased distributor orders as it moved out of its prior system into PepsiCo; FY Alani Nu retail sales +101%; ACV ramped from ~87% (start of Q4) to 94.2% by Feb 1, 2026 after the Dec 1, 2025 PepsiCo transition.
Rockstar Energy is a drag: FY retail sales -11%, TDPs -17%, 85.4% ACV, 2.4% dollar share.
International revenue grew 24% to $92.8M FY, driven by sustained Nordics growth and continued momentum in the UK, Ireland, France, Australia, New Zealand and Benelux.
The portfolio contributed 33% of the zero-sugar US energy category's $3.3B growth in 2025.
Q4 capital allocation: $197.8M of debt repayment and $39.8M of share repurchases - described as disciplined and reflecting confidence in the business.

Outlook: Alani Nu integration to complete by end of Q1 2026 and Rockstar by end of Q2 2026; gross margins expected to expand across 2026 and return to a normalized low-50s profile; the company entered 2026 'with positive momentum, scale and confidence,' citing continued strong growth across January and February 2026.

This is a press release, not a transcript - no question-and-answer session (the only quoted speaker is CEO John Fieldly). The companion same-day earnings call holds the prepared remarks and analyst Q&A.
